themes_detail.label: Public drinking surge in Harlem
themes_detail.summary: Open-container drinking complaints skyrocketed 1100% THIS WEEK to 3 reports, up from a baseline of 0.2 complaints per week over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a potential new public disorder pattern emerging in Central Harlem.
evidence: 3 drinking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Spike is statistically significant and newly emergent, not a recurring seasonal pattern
No Reddit or recent news coverage explaining the spike suggests on-the-ground reporting opportunity
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: Where are these incidents concentrated? Interview residents and local businesses about location and timing.
Policy angle: How does NYPD/Parks enforcement respond to open-container violations; has enforcement changed recently?

themes_detail.label: Park noise complaints tripling
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from parks jumped 600% LAST WEEK to 7 reports, up from a baseline of 1.0 per week, suggesting a new late-spring activity surge or event-related disruption in Central Harlem's green spaces.
evidence: 7 park noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (600% spike, z-score 4.54)
Isolated to park-specific complaints; residential noise DOWN 26% same period, suggesting localized issue
Timing coincides with warming weather and increased park usage
reporting_angles: Which parks are generating complaints? Cross-reference with event calendars or permit filings.
Resident impact: Interview park users and neighbors about what type of noise (music, gatherings, sports) and whether parks are adequately maintained/staffed.

themes_detail.label: Litter basket and dead tree spike
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests and dead/dying tree complaints each spiked 700-1100% THIS WEEK and 2 WEEKS AGO respectively, pointing to accelerating street-level maintenance and environmental concerns across Central Harlem.
evidence: Litter basket requests: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Dead/dying trees: 3 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 4.16)
Community Board budget has requested 'new equipment for maintenance' annually (Agency: Parks), indicating chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Parks maintenance backlog: Interview Parks Dept about tree inspection schedules and litter/waste bin deployment gaps in specific neighborhoods.
Environmental justice angle: Are certain blocks or parks being neglected? Map complaints against Parks capital budget allocations.

themes_detail.label: Consumer complaints rising sharply
themes_detail.summary: Consumer complaints nearly doubled (up 126%) 2 WEEKS AGO to 13 reports, up from a baseline of 5.8 per week, suggesting emerging issues with local businesses or services that warrant investigation.
evidence: 13 consumer complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 5.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (126% spike, z-score 4.06)
Complaint type is broad (consumer complaints) and requires detailed breakdown to target specific business sector
No Reddit or news coverage yet, suggesting early-stage story opportunity
reporting_angles: Data dive: Obtain detailed 311 complaint logs to categorize complaints by business type (restaurants, retail, services, etc.)
Consumer angle: Interview affected residents to identify whether spike is due to food safety issues, fraud, or service quality problems.

themes_detail.label: Abandoned bikes accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked 700% 2 WEEKS AGO to 3 reports, up from a baseline of 0.4 per week, potentially indicating theft/dumping activity or system capacity issues with bike-share infrastructure in Central Harlem.
evidence: 3 abandoned bike complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Timing suggests either seasonal increase in bike usage or localized dumping/theft problem
No concurrent news coverage suggests potential early-stage community concern
reporting_angles: Bike-share angle: Contact Citi Bike or other operators about maintenance issues, theft rates, or damaged/abandoned station bikes.
Street hazard angle: Are abandoned bikes blocking sidewalks or ADA access? Interview residents about specific locations.
